key_insight: Quantum Subspace Sampling Descent (QSSD) tackles optimization problems larger than the device’s qubit count by iteratively sampling low-energy subspaces while retaining global problem information.
engineering_relevance: QSSD offers a hardware-tested route to larger combinatorial optimization workloads without requiring one qubit per problem variable.
method: Iteratively search subspaces to decouple variable count from qubit count.
Use fixed-angle QAOA as a low-energy sampler to drive energy descent.
Precompute angles so each iteration requires one circuit execution.
evidence_signal: Tests on IBM Heron and Nighthawk devices with up to 152 qubits covered higher-order binary optimization and Max-cut; a 10,000-variable instance achieved an approximation ratio above 0.95 with 100 circuit executions.
watch_item: QSSD does not yet match the best classical baseline; its reported runtime-scaling promise does not establish quantum advantage.
paper_title: Quantum optimization beyond qubit count by low-energy subspace sampling
